title: Two Simulators, One Scenario, and the Gap Between Them Measured, Explained and Shrunk by Calibrating the Built In Model to the Other

questions.question: Why are two measures of the gap used, the largest and the end?
options: The largest is always at the end
The end is easier to compute
The end can be right while the way there was wrong
Two numbers average out the noise
questions.explanation: Two runs can finish in the same place having taken different ways there. A gap that peaks in the middle points to how the robot moves, not where it stops.

questions.question: On first order responses made with time constants of 0.05, 0.20 and 0.35 s, the reader got them back to within:
questions.explanation: The speed is taken from the distance moved in each sample, and the time it first reaches 63.2 percent of its final value is read off, interpolating between samples.

questions.question: Two built in models with lags of 0.05 and 0.30 s differed at the worst by:
options: 0.25 m, the difference of the lags
questions.explanation: Over the five cases the worst distance between the two traces was 5 cm. That is what a quarter of a second of lag is worth on these moves.

questions.question: After setting the lag read from the slower model, the gap was:
questions.explanation: The slower model's lag was read as 0.299 s and given to the faster one. The gap fell from 0.050 m to 0.0001 m, which is how a calibration is judged.

questions.question: Does calibrating one simulator to the other show which is right?
options: No: it shows what the difference is, and only the robot says which is right
Yes: the one calibrated to is right
Yes, if the gap goes to zero
questions.explanation: Two simulators made to agree can both be wrong. The procedure names the difference; the real robot decides.

questions.question: Why is each case run from rest on a freshly started world?
options: A run that starts where the last ended compares the end of one case with the start of the next
The built in model needs it
questions.explanation: Each case is meant to show one thing from rest. Carrying on from the previous case's end mixes them.
